summary: The study reports the successful growth of ordered GaInP thin films on a GaAs substrate using atomic layer epitaxy (ALE). The process involved alternating exposures to TEl, PH3, and TMGa fluxes, resulting in high-quality, smooth films with a low band gap. The films showed preferential ordering on (111) alternating planes and exhibited anomalous temperature-dependent photoluminescence behavior.
evidence: The ALE growth system was used with organometallic and hydride sources. The structure was deposited at substrate temperatures in the range 500-700°C. The ternary GaInP alloy grown at 500°C showed a peak corresponding to x ≈ 46% with a mismatch to the substrate of about 0.3%. The photoluminescence (PL) spectrum showed a sharp peak at 1.868 eV with a FWHM of about 30 meV. The temperature dependence of the near-gap PL peak energy showed anomalous behavior where the peak energy decreases, then increases with increasing temperature in the range 20-60 K.
